features.text: The patient has been experiencing high blood pressure and palpitations.
The patient had a single episode of palpitations in March, which did not recur.
The palpitations occurred during a period of stress, with excessive coffee consumption and skipped breakfast.
The patient attributes the palpitations to a panic attack.
The palpitations did not last long and were not associated with chest pain, dizziness, shortness of breath, or sweating.
The patient has no new or worsening symptoms since the last visit.
The patient is on Benicar HCT (40-25) and amlodipine 10 mg daily for hypertension.
The patient checks blood pressure every morning, with readings between 146 to 155 mmHg.
The patient is trying to cut back on salt and walks on the treadmill when possible.
The patient has a family history of hypertension, though no specific heart disease or endocrine disorders were mentioned.
The patient has not had any recent blood tests for thyroid function or catecholamines.
The patient's most recent blood test was for potassium, which was 4.0.
The patient has not undergone an ECG or Holter monitor test in the past.
The patient has not had any thyroid function tests or imaging studies in the past.
The patient's heart sounds and lungs were normal during the physical examination.
The patient did not report any swelling or pain in the ankles or feet.
The patient is willing to undergo thyroid function tests or cardiac testing if recommended.
